# tfcensus completion

Generate the autocompletion script for tfcensus for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

## Usage

```sh
tfcensus completion <shell>
```

## Shells

| Shell | Command |
|---|---|
| [bash](#bash) | `tfcensus completion bash` |
| [clink](#clink) | `tfcensus completion clink` |
| [elvish](#elvish) | `tfcensus completion elvish` |
| [fish](#fish) | `tfcensus completion fish` |
| [nushell](#nushell) | `tfcensus completion nushell` |
| [oil](#oil) | `tfcensus completion oil` |
| [powershell](#powershell) | `tfcensus completion powershell` |
| [tcsh](#tcsh) | `tfcensus completion tcsh` |
| [xonsh](#xonsh) | `tfcensus completion xonsh` |
| [zsh](#zsh) | `tfcensus completion zsh` |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command. The shell commands ignore `--format`.

### bash

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
source <(tfcensus completion bash)
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

**Linux**

```text
tfcensus completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/tfcensus
```

**macOS**

```text
tfcensus completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/tfcensus
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | disable completion descriptions | bool |  |  |  |  |

### clink

Generate the autocompletion script for clink. carapace, built into tfcensus, writes it.

Save the script as a Lua file in a clink scripts directory, such as
%LOCALAPPDATA%\clink\tfcensus.lua:

```text
tfcensus completion clink > %LOCALAPPDATA%\clink\tfcensus.lua
```

### elvish

Generate the autocompletion script for elvish. carapace, built into tfcensus, writes it.

Add this line to ~/.config/elvish/rc.elv:

```text
eval (tfcensus completion elvish | slurp)
```

### fish

Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
tfcensus completion fish | source
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

```text
tfcensus completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/tfcensus.fish
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | disable completion descriptions | bool |  |  |  |  |

### nushell

Generate the autocompletion script for nushell. carapace, built into tfcensus, writes it.

The script defines $tfcensus\_completer. Save it, source it from config.nu and use it as
the external completer (or call it from yours when the first span is tfcensus):

```text
tfcensus completion nushell | save --force ~/.config/nushell/tfcensus.nu

# config.nu
source ~/.config/nushell/tfcensus.nu
$env.config.completions.external = {enable: true, completer: $tfcensus_completer}
```

### oil

Generate the autocompletion script for oil. carapace, built into tfcensus, writes it.

Add this line to your oils startup file (~/.config/oils/oshrc or yshrc):

```text
source <(tfcensus completion oil)
```

### powershell

Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
tfcensus completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

To load completions for every new session, add the output of the above command
to your powershell profile.

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | disable completion descriptions | bool |  |  |  |  |

### tcsh

Generate the autocompletion script for tcsh. carapace, built into tfcensus, writes it.

Add this line to ~/.tcshrc:

```text
eval `tfcensus completion tcsh`
```

### xonsh

Generate the autocompletion script for xonsh. carapace, built into tfcensus, writes it.

Add this line to ~/.xonshrc:

```text
exec($(tfcensus completion xonsh))
```

### zsh

Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

```text
echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc
```

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
source <(tfcensus completion zsh)
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

**Linux**

```text
tfcensus completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_tfcensus"
```

**macOS**

```text
tfcensus completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_tfcensus
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | disable completion descriptions | bool |  |  |  |  |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
tfcensus completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/tfcensus
tfcensus completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_tfcensus"
tfcensus completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/tfcensus.fish
```
